rationale: C03 supplies an exceptionally close substantive and structural template: both proclamations recite the statutory authority for entering a bilateral trade agreement, identify two proclamations implementing it, state that the two governments agreed to termination, invoke section 350(a)'s authority to terminate implementing proclamations, and terminate both proclamations on a specified date. C24 is similarly close, including the distinctive plural-proclamation structure and the phrase “acting under and do hereby proclaim,” while C17 closely matches the mutual-agreement and termination machinery but concerns only one implementing proclamation. C03 is strongest because it combines the same President, bilateral mutual termination, and termination of two proclamations in nearly the same recital-to-operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President entered into a trade agreement with His Imperial Majesty the Shah-in-Shah of Iran ... and proclaimed such trade agreement by proclamation dated March 31, 1944 ... and the effective date thereof by proclamation dated May 29, 1944
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the President of the United States entered into a trade agreement with the President of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay ... and proclaimed such trade agreement by proclamations of November 10, 1942 ... and December 3, 1942
shared_material.explanation: Both establish the original bilateral agreement and identify two implementing proclamations in the opening recital.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Government of the United States of America and the Imperial Government of Iran have agreed to terminate such trade agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: pursuant to an agreement reached by the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay providing for the termination of the said trade agreement
shared_material.explanation: Both use a bilateral governmental agreement as the factual predicate for termination.

shared_material.child_excerpt: paragraph (6) of section 350(a) ... authorizes the President to terminate, in whole or in part, any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement entered into under such section
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the said section 350 (a) ... authorizes the President to terminate in whole or in part any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement entered into under such section
shared_material.explanation: The statutory-authority recital is materially identical.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby proclaim that the proclamations dated March 31, 1944, and May 29, 1944 ... shall terminate as of the close of August 25, 1960
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do proclaim that the said proclamations dated November 10, 1942, and December 3, 1942, are hereby terminated as of December 28, 1953
shared_material.explanation: The operative clause uses the same machinery to terminate two specifically dated proclamations on a fixed effective date.
